title: The Cornwall case
html_source: This could refer to the case involving King Edward VII, who, before his coronation, was Duke of Cornwall and Prince of Wales, and who was called on to testify on the witness stand in divorce case. It was Edward who, among other royals and nobles, seems to have started the tattoo fad during his time. It is probably more likely, however, that, given the reference to the #16, a furtive reference to homosexuality, and also, considering the verbiage to appear shortly in the paragraph about something “under their veneer in a way scarcely intended by nature… except women chiefly, who were always fiddling more or less at one another… to acts of impropriety between the two…,” that this is probably attributable to a case in 1883 in which two officials in Dublin Castle, named Cornwall and French, were publically involved in an extensive homosexual circle.
